subject: Re: SLA packaging, onboarding credits & canary coverage plan
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@brightcart.com>

Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA options + onboarding credits

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and model-routing controls look promising. Before we move further I need to reconcile two items for our procurement team:

1) A clear SLA table for uptime bands (99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99) and the associated crediting mechanism.
2) Any onboarding or ramp credits you can provide during our first 3 months while we complete canary rollouts and integration testing.

We also operate in three US regions and would like confirmation on cross-region failover coverage and whether regional failover impacts SLA credit calculations.

Can you send a short proposal with the price/commit tiers and an example amortized credit schedule? Attachments are fine.

Best,
Tom
Director of Platform Engineering
BrightCart

From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SLA options + onboarding credits

Hi Tom — thanks for the note and great meeting yesterday. Long thread cut: I put together a short proposal and attached an initial quote and a sample onboarding credit schedule (see files). High level:

- SLA bands: 99.9% (bronze), 99.95% (silver), 99.99% (gold). Each band has a transparent credit ladder (0.5%/1%/3% credits) applied to monthly invoice when SLO breached.
- Canary & onboarding credits: We can offer a phased credit pool equal to 15% of first‑quarter committed spend, released as credits on the invoice over months 1–3, contingent on a joint rollout checklist.
- Regional failover: Failover does not automatically trigger a credit. Credits are issued only for platform-wide availability shortfalls that meet our measurement criteria (we publish per-region latency & reachability metrics in Console). If a region outage causes global customer impact and a documented incident, the credit policy applies.

I flagged two ask items for you in the attached spreadsheet: expected average QPS per region, and anticipated peak concurrency. Those numbers materially affect our recommended commit tier and the size of the onboarding credit pool.

Next steps: if the numbers look reasonable, can we set a follow-up on Friday to align on commit tier and any required SOC 2 evidence for procurement? Looping in Vivek so he’s aware of the proposed concession.

Thanks,
Aisha
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-SLA-quote-BC-4472.pdf (proposal, pricing matrix); onboarding-credit-schedule.xlsx (credit amortization template)
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@brightcart.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart Sales <sales@brightcart.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options + onboarding credits

Aisha — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from procurement and engineering after reviewing doc:  

- The 15% onboarding credit is attractive; procurement wants to understand whether credits are refundable or strictly invoice‑applied. They prefer invoice credits but need a mechanism to carry over unused credits beyond month 3 if integration delays occur.
- We run two critical workloads that require a guaranteed response time for priority incidents (P1 triage within 15 minutes, P2 response within 2 hours). Can you confirm those response windows are available in the gold package or as an add‑on?
- Regarding cross‑region failover: if a US‑west outage causes routing to US‑east and we see 30% higher latency, that will still be acceptable as long as credit calculations don’t penalize us for regional routing decisions. Procurement wants explicit language that credits are tied to platform measured availability, not customer‑side routing choices.

If you can confirm the refund/carry policy and the P1/P2 commitments by end of day Friday we’ll prepare a tentative internal approval to go to legal.

Cheers,
Tom

Tom — quick internal follow-up and answers inline:  

- Credit usage & carryover: Credits are invoice‑applied by default. We can provide a one‑time carryover of unused onboarding credits up to month 6, but any carryover reduces future renewal discounts proportionally. For accounting clarity we mark onboarding credits as non‑refundable (not cash refundable).

- P1/P2 windows: Priority response add‑on is available. The gold package includes a P1 triage SLA of 30 minutes and P2 of 4 hours by default. We can contractually commit to 15 minute P1 and 2 hour P2 as a premium add‑on tied to a 12‑month reserved commit (minimum). Price impact is ~+18% over gold list for the dedicated oncall/responder roster.

- Regional failover language: We will add explicit wording that credits are assessed based on Redwood’s defined availability measurement (control‑plane and per‑region e2e probes). Customer‑initiated routing changes or edge configuration do not generate automatic credits unless they are demonstrably unrelated to the platform availability incident.

I’ve outlined two optional approaches in the attached PDF: (A) larger onboarding credit pool (20%) for a 12‑month commit, or (B) 15% pool with a P1 15‑minute oncall add‑on for a 12‑month commit. If you want, we can show an amortized bill impact comparison in Friday’s call.

Looping Priyom for billing approval on the carryover mechanism and Vivek for signoff on the margin and oncall costing.

Regards,
Aisha

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options + onboarding credits

Thanks for the context. Quick commercial constraints and recommended final position:  

- Margin floor: we can offer up to 20% onboarding credit only if BrightCart commits to a 12‑month reserved capacity with a 3‑month ramp profile. Anything above 20% requires executive approval.
- P1 15‑minute add‑on: Accepted as an offered SKU but requires a minimum monthly oncall retainer (we estimate ~12k/mo) to cover responder labor and follow‑up postmortem staffing.
- Carryover: allow up to month 6 carryover as suggested, but cap the carryover pool to 50% of the original onboarding credit. Carryover beyond month 6 is not permitted.

Priyom — please confirm billing mechanics (credit ledger treatment and renewal discount interaction). Aisha — you can present this as final unless Priyom flags material accounting issues.

Vivek
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SLA options + onboarding credits

Tom — following the internal thread, billing confirms: onboarding credits are ledgered on a per‑invoice credit line. Unused onboarding credits will carry over to subsequent invoices up to month 6 and are capped at 50% of the original pool. They are non‑refundable cash items. Renewal discounts will be calculated on net billed amounts after credits are applied.  

If that matches what BrightCart needs, Aisha and I will prepare a revised quote (BC‑4472 v2) with the 15% onboarding pool and optional P1 15‑minute add‑on pricing, plus explicit regional failover clause.

Tom — are you available Tuesday 09:00 PT for a 30‑minute alignment call? If yes, we’ll send an updated quote ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Finance & Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
